For a bottom recording bar that remains visible over other applications, install the optional display-only extension:
  mluva-overlay install
A newly installed GNOME Shell extension may require one logout and login before it can be enabled.
For automatic paste in apps without native accessibility editing, install the optional keyboard-only helper:
  mluva-input-helper install
This requires sudo once and grants same-user processes synthetic-keyboard access through an owner-only socket.
Automatic insertion is unavailable while GNOME toolkit accessibility is off.
Enable it before launching Mluva with: gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.interface toolkit-accessibility true
Applications already open when it is enabled may need to be restarted before they expose text targets.
Choose your speech and rewrite providers in Settings and supply their credentials through the application environment.
